extracted.intended_audience: prospective offerors responding to the ONR BAA for contracts and other transaction agreements (contractors, primes, subcontractors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing and submitting contract (and other transaction agreement) proposals to ONR under this BAA, including required documents, formats, certifications, compliance, reporting, and post-award obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobbying certification and SF-LLL disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must certify restrictions on use of federal funds for influencing federal officials and, if any non-Federal funds are paid to influence officers/employees of an agency or Members of Congress in connection with the award, complete and submit Standard Form-LLL, 'Disclosure Form to Report Lobbying.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification language must be included in award documents for all subawards at all tiers and all subrecipients must certify accordingly. This certification is a material representation under 31 U.S.C. 1352. Failure to file the required certification may result in civil penalties of not less than $10,000 and not more than $100,000 per failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification: prohibition on internal confidentiality agreements (GIC 19-02)
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting a proposal, the applicant represents it does not require employees, contractors, or subrecipients seeking to report fraud, waste, or abuse to sign or comply with internal confidentiality agreements that prohibit or restrict lawful reporting to designated federal investigative/law enforcement representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants agree to the full certification text by checking 'I Agree' on SF 424 (R&R) Block 17 (Supplement to financial assistance certifications and representations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification: disclosure of funding sources (Section 223(a), NDAA FY2021)
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the application, the proposing entity certifies that PIs and other key personnel have provided current, accurate, and complete current and pending support information, will update such disclosure when requested prior to award and during the award term if the agency requests, and have been made aware of Section 223(a)(1) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agrees to criminal/civil/administrative penalties for false statements (18 U.S.C. 1001). Certification is made by checking 'I Agree' on SF 424 (R&R) Block 17.

rubrics_metrics.name: General conflict of interest (COI) disclosure requirement (2 CFR 200.318(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must disclose any potential or actual scientific or non-scientific conflicts of interest for themselves and any identified subrecipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR may request more information; at its discretion ONR may require a COI mitigation plan subject to approval. Nondisclosure or misrepresentation can lead to disqualification or post-award remedial actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific conflict of interest — disclosure of collaborations and current/pending support
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific collaborations (often formed prior to submission) should be disclosed as potential conflicts; include all collaborators in the list of current and pending support even if they did not formally provide support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure helps mitigate perceived conflicts arising from close collaboration prior to application submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review for basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: For basic research proposals, ONR may use peer reviewers from academia, industry, and Government to periodically appraise performance and determine continued funding eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-government peer reviewers must sign nondisclosure agreements before receiving copies of proposals/reports. Offerors may include PI travel costs to attend peer review. Peer reviews may consider information from project/program review meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on certain telecommunications and video surveillance services/equipment (PL 115-232, §889)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients and subrecipients are prohibited from using award funds to procure/extend/renew contracts for covered telecommunications equipment or services (e.g., equipment produced by Huawei, ZTE, Hytera, Hangzhou Hikvision, Dahua) or equipment/services from entities believed to be owned/controlled by a covered foreign country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered foreign country is defined as the People’s Republic of China. See Public Law 115-232, section 889 for additional details and specific prohibited items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency assistance to transition from covered equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: In implementing the prohibition under PL 115-232, heads of executive agencies shall prioritize available funding and technical support to assist affected entities to transition from covered communications equipment and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritization includes assistance to procure replacement equipment and ensure continued service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award reporting: applicability threshold (2 CFR Part 200 Appendix XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Federal share of any award may include more than $500,000 over the period of performance, the post-award reporting requirements for Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Award Terms and Conditions require reporting as described in the subsequent Reporting of Matters related to Recipient Integrity and Performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of matters related to recipient integrity and performance (FAPIIS/SAM)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the total value of an entity's currently active Federal grants, cooperative agreements, and procurement contracts exceeds $10,000,000 at any time during the award period, the recipient must maintain current information reported to SAM and the designated integrity and performance system (FAPIIS) about certain civil, criminal, or administrative proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information posted after April 15, 2011 (except past performance reviews for procurement contracts) will be publicly available. This is a statutory requirement under 41 U.S.C. 2313.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings required to be reported (types and thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report proceedings that are connected to Federal award performance, reached final disposition within the most recent five-year period, and meet one of: criminal conviction; civil finding of fault with monetary penalty/fine/restitution of $5,000 or more; administrative proceeding resulting in fault/liability and payment of $5,000 or more or reimbursement/restitution/damages over $100,000; or other proceedings that could have led to such outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also report proceedings with dispositions by consent/compromise acknowledging fault if reporting does not conflict with applicable laws/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting procedures and frequency for integrity matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter required information about proceedings into the SAM Entity Management area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients subject to the reporting requirement must report information for the most recent five-year period, either to add new proceedings or to affirm there is no new information. Entities with cumulative Federal awards > $10,000,000 must disclose semiannually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions used for reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions provided include: administrative proceeding (non-judicial adjudicatory process), conviction (judgment of criminal offense by court of competent jurisdiction, includes nolo contendere), and 'total value of currently active grants...' (only the Federal share and includes expected increments/options).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions guide what must be reported under the integrity and performance term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete proposal package: required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete proposal package must include: (1) Cover page (pdf), (2) Proposal Checklist (pdf), (3) Technical Proposal Template (Word), (4) Cost Proposal Template (Excel) for prime and all proposed subcontractors, (5) DCAA Pre-award Survey (pdf) if contractor lacks approved accounting system, (6) Statement of Work (SOW) (Word), (7) ONR Contract Specific Representations and Certifications (pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items 1–6 are located on the ONR website and contain embedded instructions. Attachments can be incorporated into the Proposal Checklist. FedConnect will not accept a proposal unless the Cover Sheet is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document format requirements (paper, margins, spacing, font, file types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper Size 8.5 x 11 inches; margins 1 inch; spacing single or double; font Times New Roman 12-point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All documents except Cost Proposal Spreadsheet and SOW must be submitted in secure, pdf-compatible format. The Cost Proposal Spreadsheet must be Microsoft Excel compatible and the SOW must be Microsoft Word. Attachments to required documents must be secure, pdf-compatible. Secure PDF is intended to prevent unauthorized editing; do not require a password to open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of technical data/computer software rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must submit a separate list of all technical data or computer software to be furnished to the Government with other-than-unlimited rights as part of the Proposal Checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Government will assume unlimited rights if offerors fail to identify any intellectual property restrictions. Include all proprietary claims to results, prototypes, and/or deliverables. If no restrictions are intended, state 'NONE.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified acquisitions and small proposals (≤ $250K) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals at or below the simplified acquisition threshold (≤ $250,000), the Technical Proposal Template, Proposal Checklist, and Cost Proposal Spreadsheet are required. Purchase orders may contain options as long as base plus options ≤ $250K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required templates and spreadsheets are completed for small-value proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontract cost proposal requirements (> $250K)
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed subcontracts or inter-organizational transfers over $250,000, offerors must provide a separate, fully completed Cost Proposal Spreadsheet for each subcontractor with supporting documentation, provided with the prime’s proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If subcontract information is proprietary, it may be submitted via e-mail to the Program Officer; e-mail must identify proposal title, prime Offeror, indicate the attachment is a subcontract, and include a description of the subcontract effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options pricing and task-level cost breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed options identified but not fully priced in the Cost Proposal Spreadsheet will not be included in any resulting contract. Options must be separately priced with separate spreadsheets for the base period and each option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a summary by period of performance (base and options) and a breakdown of cost for each task in the SOW. The sum of all costs by task worksheets MUST equal the total cost summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excel cost spreadsheet 'useable condition' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Excel spreadsheet must be in 'useable condition' to aid Government evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Useable condition' means the spreadsheet should visibly include and separately identify within each appropriate cell any and all inputs, formulas, calculations, etc.; do not provide 'value only' spreadsheets (i.e., cell values without formulas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed fee guidance and Technology Incentive (TI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government objective for fixed fees is set per DFARS 215.404-71. The solicitation provides ranges and normal values by contract risk factor and contract type; TI is rarely used at ONR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically, the range of fee is 5% to 7.5% on an ONR-awarded contract. Assign weights to Technical and Management/Cost Control so the total equals 100%; normal and range values vary by contract type and risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission portals and registration (FedConnect and MCWL)
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR uses FedConnect for submission of full proposals for contracts and other transaction agreements; Marine Corps Warfighting Lab (MCWL) accepts only electronic submissions by email to specified addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To use FedConnect, obtain a DUNS number, register with SAM (sam.gov), and create a FedConnect account. If first person in organization to register in FedConnect, SAM MPIN is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: FedConnect assistance and question submission guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: FedConnect Support Team contact information provided (support@fedconnect.net; 1-800-899-6665; Mon–Fri 8 a.m.–8 p.m. EDT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the FedConnect Message Center to submit questions; email the POCs identified in Section G (Federal Awarding Agency Contacts). ONR FAQ is available on their website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient qualifications and responsibility (FAR 9.104-1 and FAPIIS checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts shall be awarded only to responsible prospective contractors as defined in FAR 9.104-1; applicants should provide information to assist the Contracting Officer in evaluating responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAPIIS will be checked prior to award. Applicants may comment in FAPIIS on information entered by government officials. FAPIIS information will be used to judge integrity, business ethics, and performance record affecting award determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-furnished property and facilities (GFE) identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Government research facilities and operational military units may be available as GFE/facilities; offerors should consider these resources and indicate which facilities are critical for project success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate required facilities in the Proposal Checklist, Section II, Block 9. Use of GFE will be negotiated as program unfolds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of arms, ammunition and explosives (AA&E) — safety and security requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If AA&E will be utilized, the Offeror must comply with DoD manual 4145.26-M (DoD Contractor’s Safety Manual for Ammunition and Explosives) and obtain a preaward safety survey from the cognizant DCMA office before proposal submission; include required preaward safety surveys with proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offeror is also responsible for preaward security surveys (DoD 5100.76-M) and must provide written AA&E accountability procedures if required. Government may require perimeter fencing. Certain government-provided A&E with nitrocellulose-based propellants may invoke NMCARS clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAM and E-Verify clauses incorporated
rubrics_metrics.description: FAR 52.204-7 (System for Award Management) and FAR 52.204-13 (SAM Maintenance) are incorporated; FAR-based procurement contracts require enrollment in E-Verify and inclusion of FAR 52.222-54 (Employment Eligibility Verification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure organizational registration and maintenance in SAM and compliance with employment eligibility verification where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) disclosures and mitigation plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must state whether they are aware of any actual or potential OCI (FAR 2.101 and FAR Subpart 9.5) for themselves and proposed subcontractors/partners/consultants/affiliates. Those providing support services to ONR or aware of circumstances that could create an unfair competitive advantage must submit detailed information and a Mitigation Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation Plan must at minimum include: organizational charts showing structure and elements creating OCI; demonstration of isolation of OCI elements from performance resources; geographic/physical separation info; personnel reassignment process for relevant contracts/agreements; controls (including nondisclosure agreements) over future employment of departing employees; OCI training details (timing, frequency, length, content); and evidence that asserted facts mitigate OCI concerns. Offerors not providing support services should include a certification statement that no OCI exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCI review, remedies, and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer will review OCI certifications, statements, and Mitigation Plans and may request additional information. If an OCI exists, the Government may impose conditions to avoid conflict, disqualify the offeror, award with mitigating conditions, or seek a waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an actual or significant potential OCI cannot be reasonably avoided, neutralized or mitigated, the offeror will be ineligible for award. If accepted, the Mitigation Plan becomes part of the contract. Failure to disclose required OCI information results in disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data (TINA) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that meet the Truth in Negotiations Act (TINA) threshold are subject to certified cost and pricing data; offerors must execute the Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data as soon as practicable but no later than five business days after the date of price agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any cost/pricing data submitted after price agreement will be reviewed after award to determine whether certified data previously submitted was defective and whether the Government is entitled to a price adjustment under FAR 52.215-10 or FAR 52.215-11. See OUSD memorandum on eliminating inefficiencies associated with post-price-agreement submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrative list of FAR/DFARS/NMCARS provisions/clauses that may be incorporated
rubrics_metrics.description: The solicitation lists numerous FAR, DFARS, and NMCARS provisions and clauses that may be applicable to resulting ONR contracts (e.g., 52.204-7/13/16/24/25/26, 52.215-20/16/22, 52.216 series, 52.222 series, 252.204-7012, 252.204-7019/7020, 252.204-7018, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR reserves the right to include any relevant and current clauses required in the final award; offerors should be prepared to comply with applicable clauses referenced and check the solicitation for the final clause list.
